item.title: Trump threatens Oman, Iran war in stalemate as 60-day talks window ends
item.description: The 60-day deadline for the U.S. and Iran to negotiate a peace deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz is expiring, with no agreement in sight.

item.title: CBS News poll on whether Democrats split over socialism
item.description: Americans think more young people in office would make politics better.

item.title: Suge Knight could testify in trial of man accused of ordering Tupac's murder
item.description: Marion Hugh "Suge" Knight Jr., who cofounded Death Row Records, is on the witness list in the trial of the man accused of ordering Tupac Shakur's murder, which begins Monday. Celebrity attorney Chris Melcher has more.

item.title: What the U.S.-Iran stalemate means for oil prices
item.description: The U.S. and Iran remain in a stalemate as the 60-day negotiation period expires, and access to the Strait of Hormuz remains unclear. Emily Peck, a markets correspondent for Axios, joins with more.

item.title: Cost of school supplies skyrockets amid Trump's tariffs and Iran war
item.description: The cost of school supplies has skyrocketed this year amid the war in Iran and President Trump's aggressive tariff policy. Tibor Besedes, an economics professor at the Georgia Institute of Technology, joins with more.

item.title: Watch Live: Prosecution rests in Lindsay Clancy murder trial, defense to take over
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's Massachusetts murder trial is back underway Monday in Plymouth Superior Court with a fourth week of witness testimony.

item.title: Senior Israeli official calls for killing of "30 to 40" Gazans every night
item.description: Israel's far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir calls for nightly "targeted assassinations" in Gaza: "They're not even people."

item.title: Can debt collectors garnish your 401(k) if you owe money?
item.description: A debt collection judgment can have serious consequences. Here's what it could mean for your retirement funds.

item.title: Trump's former Middle East ambassador on Iran as 60-day negotiation period expires
item.description: James Jeffrey, a former U.S. diplomat and deputy national security adviser under three administrations, including President Trump's first term, joins to discuss where U.S.-Iran relations stand as the 60-day negotiation period expires.

item.title: Races to watch as Florida gears up for primaries, including election for DeSantis replacement
item.description: Florida is set to hold primary elections on Tuesday, including a highly contested Republican gubernatorial primary to replace Rob DeSantis. CBS News Miami's Jim DeFede breaks down some key races to watch.

item.title: Blanche refuses to pledge DOJ's independence from Trump
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche refused to pledge that the Department of Justice would remain independent of President Trump and the White House, despite decades of precedent. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: BBC asks court to subpoena Trump family members for defamation defense
item.description: After failing to deliver subpoenas itself, the BBC has asked a Florida court to compel three of President Trump's family members to testify over the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol.

item.title: Trump family crypto firm granted conditional approval to establish a bank
item.description: The plan has sparked criticism from Democrats, who argue that granting bank status to a business affiliated with the Trump family poses a conflict of interest.

item.title: What to know about murder trial of Tupac Shakur ahead of opening statements
item.description: Opening statements are expected to begin Monday in Las Vegas in the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, the man accused of orchestrating the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in 1996. Davis has pleaded not guilty. CBS News legal analyst Caroline Polisi breaks down what to expect.

item.title: CENTCOM commander meets with troops on USS Abraham Lincoln amid concerns for sailors' mental health
item.description: U.S. Central Command chief, Admiral Brad Cooper, met with troops on the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose historic deployment is raising concerns for the service members' mental health. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has the latest.

item.title: Jon Batiste on the "flow state" of creating 3 albums at once and piano as a "form of meditation"
item.description: Jon Batiste speaks with "CBS Mornings" about his three new albums, which were inspired by composers Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and Thelonious Monk, and explains how he crafted each one in a single day. The Grammy winner also gives an update on his wife, who is battling cancer.

item.title: Ukraine's recently fired defense minister describes the "technological war" with Russia
item.description: Former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov is breaking down the technological efforts from both sides in the Russia-Ukraine war. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: CENTCOM commander tries to ease concerns about USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have disputed concerns about conditions aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln.

item.title: Writer behind viral essay about getting a facelift on making a feminist case for plastic surgery
item.description: An opinion essay in the New York Times is sparking conversation about feminism and the growing normalization of plastic surgery. Molly Jong-Fast, an author and political commentator, discusses her decision to have a facelift at 47 and if it makes her a "bad feminist."

item.title: U.K. prime minister messages with impersonator of top Trump staffer
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham exchanged messaged with someone pretending to be White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.

item.title: Republican, Democratic strategists weigh in on split over socialism
item.description: Recent CBS News polling shows how Americans feel about socialism as shifts within the Democratic Party become more prevalent. Political strategists Joel Payne and Samir Kapadia join CBS News with more.

item.title: How an Amazon driver's routine delivery led to a special connection with a military family
item.description: During her shift, an Amazon driver in Kentucky took a moment to untangle an American flag. CBS News contributor David Begnaud shows how the routine delivery turned into a special moment with a military family.

item.title: Tips to help you pack your child's school lunch this year
item.description: Registered dietitian Megan McNamee weighs in on how to make your child's school lunch easier and more affordable as kids head back to the classroom.

item.title: Former Hurricane Lala drenches Hawaii, flash floods sweep away Big Island homes
item.description: Lala was weakening but still packing a punch as it moved away from the islands, forecasters said.

item.title: Lala slammed Hawaii as hurricane with pounding rain and strong winds
item.description: Lala slammed Hawaii over the weekend after briefly becoming a hurricane. CBS News' Jonathan Vigliotti looks at the damage.

item.title: Supreme Court won't rehear Trump's appeal of $5 million E. Jean Carroll case
item.description: The Supreme Court declined for the second time to consider President Trump's appeal in the E. Jean Carroll case.

item.title: Trump's son-in-law met with Hamas leaders in Egypt over Gaza peace plan
item.description: Jared Kushner, one of President Trump's negotiators on Middle East matters, met with Hamas leaders in Egypt to discuss the latest progress in the U.S.-backed Gaza peace deal. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere dies at 36
item.description: Actor Hayden Panettiere, known for her roles in "Remember the Titans" and "Heroes," has died at 36, her publicist confirmed. CBS News' Bradley Blackburn reports.

item.title: RFK Jr.'s hunt for autism culprits stalls amid Trump's baseless vaccine order
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s closed-door research has yet to produce evidence linking vaccines and autism.

item.title: Jared Kushner met with Hamas leaders in Egypt to discuss Gaza peace deal
item.description: Jared Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law, is set to meet next with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who rejected the latest peace proposal last week.
